agree.reason: Dana's own $600K figure opens the email, and a concrete before-and-after result makes a 20-minute call an easy yes, but nothing ties the $75K cost to her savings, and nothing gives her a line to take to her IT director.

honest.reason: It drops the 'cut errors in half' claim and gives the pet-supply numbers accurately, but it shows only the best of six customers and leaves out the 2.8-to-2.2 result, so the single case reads as more typical than the facts support.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out $75,000 a year for five sites, but it never states the 54% reduction or what that would mean against her $600K (about $320K a year, a payback of roughly 4 to 1), which is the strongest true figure available.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo of $600K+ a year in returns appears in the opening line, but it never comes back as the alternative to set against the $75K price.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is 'see whether those numbers could hold up in your buildings', which is vague and gives her no number, timeframe or checkpoint she could test, such as a mis-pick rate after five months at one site.

objections.reason: Saying it doesn't replace the WMS and runs on top of it speaks to the IT director's resistance, but it doesn't say how little IT work or integration is needed, which is what he would actually object to.

fit.reason: It is short and plain, with brief paragraphs that read easily on a phone, as the brief asked.
